symptom: A caller-controlled descriptor proxy could expose one Ed25519 public key during mathematical signature verification and a different public key during later claimed-anchor or synthetic-reference key-digest correlation. Both metadata correlation flags could otherwise describe a key that did not verify the signature. Independent authority and scoring were never granted.
lesson: Rebinding a rebuilt request transcript is not sufficient when the Ed25519 claim itself is read again. A proxy can change claimedPublicKeySpkiPem after signature verification, so later role/key or reference comparisons must use the same claim snapshot that was mathematically checked.
guardrail: Take a strict own-data-descriptor snapshot of the complete untrusted signature claim before the first math check; pass that immutable primitive-value snapshot through claimed-anchor and synthetic-reference correlation. Do not reread the original caller claim after verification. Preserve literal independentAuthorityVerified=false and scoringAuthorized=false on all paths.
